title: Yes-but: Text 2 accepts Text 1 and adds a limit
subtitle: Cross-Text Connections · 9 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **9 of the official questions in Cross-Text Connections are this one** — 0 Easy, 6 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Text 2 starts by crediting Text 1's work ('certainly offer encouraging insight', 'have shown that', 'deserved attention') and then turns on 'but', 'still', or 'it's important to consider'.
- The question asks for Text 2's response.
- The right choice sounds partly agreeing, e.g. 'would agree... but caution that...' or 'would note that this may not apply to...'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Mark the concession clause and the pivot word in Text 2.
- 2) Name what Text 2 adds after the pivot: a cost Text 1 left out, a case where it doesn't hold, a longer time frame, or a missing mechanism.
- 3) Choose the option that keeps Text 1's point and adds that limit.
- Reject options that throw Text 1 out entirely.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You treat any 'but' as full disagreement and pick the choice where Text 2 dismisses Text 1.
That discards the concession Text 2 explicitly made.
The reverse mistake is picking pure agreement and ignoring the caveat.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
